page: Microsoft Azure E16-4ds_v6 is a constrained-core memory-optimized virtual machine provisioned on Microsoft Hyper-V. It is powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8573C processor clocked at 4.2 GHz, allocating 4 dedicated vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores with hyperthreading. The configuration delivers an expansive 128.0 GB of system memory, yielding an extraordinarily high ratio of 32.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Hardware acceleration instructions include AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX). Bundled ephemeral storage is provided via a direct-attached 944 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance operates without a discrete GPU.

Benchmark evaluation shows polarized compute metrics resulting from the low core count combined with high clock frequencies. Single-core throughput is prominent, registering a Geekbench single-core score of 2093.0 in the upper quartile. Conversely, aggregate compute is restricted by the 4-vCPU ceiling, as reflected by a multi-core Geekbench score of 4739.0 and a multi-core stress-ng result of 3948.96. Memory subsystem performance remains modest under saturation, exhibiting large-block uncached read speeds of 34.95 GB/sec and write speeds of 24.77 GB/sec. Static web throughput achieves 7.39 GB/sec, while Redis SET performance peaks at 5.57 million operations per second.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the E16-4ds_v6 functions as a specialized deployment for software licensing optimization. Applications licensed on a per-core basis, such as commercial relational databases, benefit from accessing 128 GB of RAM and local NVMe scratch storage without incurring the software licensing fees of a full 16-core footprint. Tradeoffs center on limited parallel compute capacity and lower multi-threaded throughput, precluding this profile from demanding parallel compilation, heavy batch processing, or large-scale machine learning inference. Recommended workloads include memory-heavy relational database engines, large in-memory caching systems, and enterprise data analytics tasks constrained by per-core licensing.
description: Microsoft Azure E16-4ds_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine tailored for memory-dense environments requiring minimized core counts. Running on the x86_64 Intel Xeon 8573C processor at 4.2 GHz, the instance delivers 4 dedicated vCPUs across 2 physical cores alongside an expansive 128.0 GB of RAM, equating to 32.0 GB per vCPU. Storage needs are supported by an integrated 944 GB local NVMe SSD, with zero discrete GPUs attached. Benchmark assessments demonstrate strong single-core speed, evidenced by a Geekbench score of 2093.0, though overall multi-threaded throughput is restricted by the 4-thread execution cap. The resource architecture offers favorable cost efficiency for memory-intensive enterprise software governed by per-core licensing constraints. It is predominantly matched for memory-resident relational databases, large caches, and specialized data transformation workloads requiring vast RAM buffers alongside modest parallel compute.
